title: Historical RTEC AAP annual audit, reporting and goal-setting cycle
ownership: EEO Manager develops and prepares formal AAP documents and is responsible for effective implementation.
Department managers and supervisors share responsibility for implementation and reporting problem areas.
Executive Director receives status reporting, discusses significant issues with the EEO Manager and remains the senior accountability point.
Historical AAP administration language also calls for at least semiannual EEO reporting to the Executive Director on departmental progress and contractor/vendor compliance.
audit_purposes: Measure effectiveness of the AAP/EEO program.
Identify problem areas requiring remedial action.
Determine the extent to which goals and objectives were achieved.
annual_review_domains: recruitment, selection, advertising and job-application procedures
hiring, promotion, transfers, layoffs and termination
job assignments, classifications, job descriptions and seniority lists
sick leave, leaves of absence and other leave
training, apprenticeships, professional meetings and conferences
other terms, conditions and privileges of employment
issue_escalation: Managers/supervisors are asked to report current or foreseeable EEO problem areas and propose solutions.
Problem areas are to be reported immediately to the EEO Manager.
The EEO Manager discusses issues such as significant rejection ratios and EEO charges with the Executive Director.
The EEO Manager reports goal/objective status and recommends remedial actions.
utilization_and_goal_method: Annually identify job areas in which women/minorities are underutilized.
Compare actual workforce representation with availability in the relevant/applicable labor market.
The 2018-2024 source describes an underutilization test based on the difference between availability and workforce percentage multiplied by job-group headcount, with .5-or-greater rounding.
Establish annual good-faith goals based on the identified gaps and expected openings/turnover.
Document annual incumbency, availability, personnel activity and narrative/good-faith efforts.
Review the next period against prior goals, including gross additions and turnover losses.
currentness_boundary: This is a historical AAP process model derived from plans through June 2024; it is not proof of the current post-2024 AAP methodology.
Historical hiring-screening and self-identification language embedded in the AAP must not be reused automatically as current forms or criteria.
Historical percentage/formula anomalies documented in the 2022 AAP must be resolved before automating availability/goal calculations.
automation_candidates: Versioned annual AAP compiler pulling from restricted HR data into privacy-safe aggregate tables.
Deterministic formula validation and count/percentage consistency checks before goals are approved.
Year-over-year normalized job-group comparison that applies known EEO-1 remapping.
Automated variance report: prior goals vs hires/terminations/transfers/net representation.
Semiannual compliance dashboard for management with evidence links and exception flags.
Document-generation pipeline that separates restricted source rows from safe AAP aggregate outputs.
